r: Most new graduates assume the first offer is final, but it rarely is. Recruiters typically budget 5–10% of headroom above the opening figure, and the first number spoken tends to anchor everything after it, so let the employer name theirs first. Use salary band data from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, or the BLS Occupational Outlook to plan your counter, ideally landing near the band's 75th percentile. Candidates who accept the opening offer without a single counter pay a silence tax. A $5,000 shortfall, compounded by 3% annual raises, grows to more than $370,000 over a 40-year career. Babcock's Carnegie Mellon research found that only 7% of women negotiated, compared with 57% of men, and the offer letter quietly turns that gap into lifetime earnings differences. Send your counter by email and cite market evidence rather than personal need. If base pay stalls, treat signing bonuses, equity, and start dates as extra currency you can trade.
